title: AI Payroll Software: What AI Actually Automates in Payroll (and What to Verify)
summary: See how AI automates the time-off, expense and shift-swap decisions behind accurate payroll, and how to tell built-in AI from a paid add-on.
body_markdown:
When you evaluate AI in payroll software, ask:


- Which decisions that feed payroll does the software automate?
- How does it automate decisions?
- Which decisions and processes still go to a person?
- How are employees alerted to possible paycheck errors before payroll is submitted?
- Is the AI built into the software, or added on top?


## What is AI in payroll software?


AI payroll software automates the routine decisions and processes behind each pay cycle. Some payroll software automates the pay run itself. AI makes payroll more accurate by automating the decisions that influence payroll calculations (like for time-off requests, punch changes and expense reimbursements) and flagging errors *before* submission.


The most useful form is automated decisioning logic: decision engines that evaluate routine requests by applying your company’s rules the same way every time, without human intervention. Other AI models handle other jobs; for example, vision language models read receipts, and natural language processing answers employee questions.


Automation describes what happens. The AI model describes how it happens. An approved time-off request and a paycheck flagged for review are both automated, but they’re different decisions made in different ways.


## Challenge 1: Payroll inputs depend on decisions


Every pay cycle is influenced by decisions made even before a payroll cycle begins, including time-off, expense and shift-swap approvals. When those decisions must wait on a manager, payroll waits, too. AI can automate them.


### *What does AI in payroll processing automate?*


Three of payroll’s biggest inputs depend on decisions:


1. **Time-off data:** Each request has to be approved or denied before the hours reach payroll.
2. **Expense reimbursements:** Each receipt has to be reviewed and the amount approved before it’s paid.
3. **Hours worked by shift:** Shift-swap and punch change requests have to be approved before a timecard can accurately reflect hours worked.


Each of those decisions drives unnecessary costs when handled by hand. 2025 research by[EY estimates](https://eyquest.com/Files/HR_Benchmarking_Study_White_Paper_2025.pdf) that for companies that don’t use self-service HR software, reviewing and approving one time-off request costs $12.15, approving one shift swap costs $15.06 and reviewing one expense request’s supporting documentation costs $13.53. Those costs repeat with every request.


At Shamin Hotels, a hotel operator with over 3,000 associates, those inputs were once processed through the HR team by hand. “My HR and payroll team would spend about 50% of their day working on direct deposit updates, time punch edits, PTO requests, address updates, I-9 identification uploads,” said Shannon Flynn, vice president of human resources.


A late approval doesn’t just clutter an inbox. It becomes a correction *after* an employee gets paid.


### *How does automated decisioning keep payroll inputs accurate?*


Automated decisioning logic applies the rules an organization sets to incoming requests. Here’s what that looks like in Paycom’s software, based on its[published decision inventory](https://www.paycom.com/ai-standards/) :


**Payroll input** **Decision automated** **AI model behind it**


Time off Time-off approval or denial by company policy (Time-Off Requests featuring GONE®) Automated decision engine


Timecards and punches Timecard approval or denial, and punch-change approval or denial (Time and Attendance) Automated decision engine


Shifts Shift-swap approval or denial by your criteria (Scheduling) Automated decision engine


Expenses Expense approval up to an amount you set, with uploaded receipts read to prefill the request (Expense Management) Automated decision engine and vision language model


Benefits Initial benefit-plan enrollment approval (Benefits Administration) Automated decision engine


Direct deposit Direct deposit return resolution determination (Client Action Center) Automated decision engine


Leave management Approval of intermittent leave based on criteria you set Automated decision engine


Every rule is yours to set and update, and every decision stays visible and reversible by a person. Because each decision reads the same employee record in a single database, a time-off decision, a timecard approval and a paycheck all work from one source of truth instead of several reconciled systems.


**Before:** A manager reviews every request, checks the policy, records a decision and waits for the data to reach payroll.


**After:** Routine requests are automatically approved or denied by your rules, and the approved data flows into payroll.


**Customer result:** After moving HR and payroll into a single database, with tools including Beti®, Time and Attendance, Scheduling and Time-Off Requests featuring GONE,[Shamin Hotels](https://www.paycom.com/learn-more/hospitality-case-study/) reduced payroll processing time by 85%.


## Challenge 2: Payroll errors surface after employees are paid


Automation helps catch errors before payroll submission by guiding employees to access, review, troubleshoot, verify and approve their own pay, so issues get resolved *before* they force retroactive corrections.


### *How does payroll automation catch errors before submission?*


Automation doesn’t complete every payroll action. Employees still review and approve their pay. What automation does is find and flag possible errors early.


In an[automated payroll experience](https://www.paycom.com/software/beti/) , payroll starts itself each period and pulls in live data from timecards, expenses, time off, benefits and any other area that impacts employee pay. When the software finds a possible error, it alerts the employee, who is guided to review it, fix it and approve the paycheck, all before payroll is submitted.


Catching errors before submission means fewer time-consuming, costly corrections and uncomfortable explanations after payday. EY estimates that processing one off-cycle payroll by hand costs $14.54.


### *Where do AI answers fit around the pay cycle?*


Answers generated from AI can be relevant before, during and after payroll. Before payroll runs, an employee might check a time-off balance or a manager might approve a punch change. During payroll, an employee might verify their benefits elections. After payroll, an employee might ask about a pay stub.


IWant™, Paycom’s command-driven AI engine, answers these questions from permission-based data in a single database. It doesn’t process payroll, but gets employees and managers answers so routine questions don’t overwhelm HR.


A commissioned[Forrester Consulting](https://www.paycom.com/resources/total-economic-impact-paycom-iwant/) study of IWant, conducted on behalf of Paycom in February 2026, projected up to 431% three-year ROI for a composite organization based on interviewed customers.* “As an executive, IWant saves me at least a few hours a day,” said Nirav Patel, regional director of operations at Shamin Hotels.


## Challenge 3: What does employee AI usage really cost?


AI’s real cost depends on whether it’s built into the software or added on top. Embedded AI can come at no extra cost. AI that’s added on may carry separate charges that grow as your workforce uses it.


### *How do vendors price AI in payroll software?*


AI pricing has become part of the payroll software decision, and it isn’t always easy to compare. Ask each vendor to identify:


- the core payroll and HR functions
- any separate AI add-on or module
- per-user or per-employee AI token charges
- usage-based charges or credit allowances
- renewal terms that could change any of the above


Then compare those terms with how you’ll actually use the software. As more managers rely on automated approvals? As decisions run every pay period? Every year?


If your costs grow exponentially every time an approval is automated, you’ll feel pressure to automate less. Less automation means more manual decisions delaying payroll.


### *Embedded AI*


Paycom’s smart AI, including its automated decisioning, is built into its core HR and payroll functionality, and the company[doesn’t charge additional costs for AI usage](https://www.paycom.com/ai-standards/) . It builds its own software on a single database and self-hosts client data on its own premises, duplicated across multiple facilities nationwide.


As you compare vendors, ask who builds the AI, where it runs and who owns that infrastructure. The answers affect how your data is handled and whether your AI costs stay predictable.


## Challenge 4: Automation and AI don’t replace human oversight


AI handles routine decisions impacting payroll calculations, and HR keeps oversight and control by setting the rules.


### *Does artificial intelligence in payroll replace human review?*


No. Employees are guided to review and approve their own paychecks. Managers can reverse an automated decision in the event of an emergency or exception that falls outside regular company policy. Your team also ultimately decides what the rules are and when they change.


Your obligations stay the same too.[The U.S. Department of Labor](https://www.dol.gov/general/topic/wages/wagesrecordkeeping) requires covered employers to keep accurate records of hours worked and wages earned for covered, nonexempt workers. The[IRS](https://www.irs.gov/businesses/small-businesses-self-employed/outsourcing-payroll-and-third-party-payers) reminds employers that they’re generally still ultimately responsible for withheld income tax and Social Security and Medicare taxes when they outsource payroll duties.


That responsibility grows with your footprint. “Every state comes with their own challenges,” said Flynn. Before you go live, confirm the software handles every state, entity and country you pay in. Beti, for example, is available in the U.S., Mexico, Canada, the U.K. and Ireland.


### *What oversight should automated decisions include?*


Every automated decision should be visible, explainable and reversible by a person. Before you go live, confirm:


- who sets the decision rules and who can change them
- how a manager reviews or reverses an automated approval
- what happens to decisions and processes that fall outside your rules


The U.S.[National Institute of Standards and Technology (NIST) AI Risk Management Framework](https://www.nist.gov/itl/ai-risk-management-framework) offers voluntary guidance on building trustworthiness into the design, development, use and evaluation of AI, which provides useful background for these questions.


## Automated payroll evaluation checklist


To evaluate automated payroll software, confirm which decisions its AI automates and how they impact payroll, how it identifies paycheck errors before submission and whether the AI is embedded or added on. Use this checklist to compare vendors. For every answer, ask for a demonstration or the relevant contract language.


**Evaluation area** **Question to ask** **Evidence to request**


Payroll automation Which payroll steps run automatically each pay cycle? A full pay-cycle demonstration


Input decisions Which time-off, expense and shift decisions are automated? The decision rules and a live example of each


AI processing Which AI model makes each automated decision? A mapping of each decision to its model type


Data source Does every decision read one employee record? Where the data comes from and any steps to reconcile it


Error detection How are employees alerted to possible payroll errors? A demonstration of the alert and how it’s resolved


Employee review Do employees review and approve paychecks? The approval range settings and the approval workflow


Human oversight Who has the ability to control what decisions are automated and changed when necessary? The paths for correction and reversal


Workforce complexity Does automated payroll cover every state, entity and country you pay in? A demonstration using your own jurisdictions


Embedded or added on Is AI embedded into the software or added on top? Written pricing showing what capabilities are included


Cost predictability Does cost change as automated decisions grow? Written terms covering usage, head count and renewal


A strong vendor answer shows you how its AI makes automated payroll more accurate, not just which features carry an AI label.


## Frequently asked questions about AI payroll software


### *Does AI automate payroll?*


In modern payroll software, the pay run is already automated. AI improves that automation by deciding routine inputs, such as time-off, expense and shift-swap approvals and by alerting employees to possible paycheck errors — and guiding employees to resolve them — before payroll is submitted.


### *What is automated decisioning in payroll?*


Automated decisioning logic is a form of AI that applies your company’s rules to routine requests the same way every time. Each decision stays visible to and reversible by a person. These decisions provide the timely, accurate information needed to automatically calculate payroll.


### *Does AI approve paychecks?*


No. When the software finds a possible error, it guides the employee to review, troubleshoot and resolve it, then approve the paycheck before payroll is submitted.


### *Is AI in payroll software embedded or added on?*


It depends on the vendor. Ask whether the AI is embedded in the software or a separate add-on, and get the pricing terms in writing.


### *Does AI payroll software cost extra?*


Some vendors charge separately for AI, or charge based on how much it’s used. Paycom doesn’t charge additional costs for AI usage, including its automated decisioning.


### *Does AI replace payroll staff?*


No. Automation and AI take over repetitive decisions. People still set the rules, review paychecks, reverse automated decisions and keep oversight.
